summary: Independent adversarial re-review of the R2-4 bootstrap merge gate, performed on a fresh context over bundle bytes only, treating every supplied PASS as an unverified claim. Integrity is fully reproduced: the bundle SHA-256 (24e35ecf...), REVIEW_MANIFEST (5aae77da...), BOOTSTRAP_MERGE_GATE_EVIDENCE (7dd8186e...) and GATE_SOURCE (8c9da499...) all match, all 26 manifest entries verify on path, digest and byte count, and the ZIP contains no unlisted file. All three diff objects were rebuilt independently: main..anchor is 16 records, anchor..HEAD is exactly 2, main..HEAD is 17, and anchor composed with tail reproduces the full record set exactly on every path, action, mode and object identifier. Every Git blob identifier was recomputed from bytes and matched: 17 of 17 at HEAD, 5 of 5 at the anchor, plus main's R2_STATE.md. Actions are confined to add and modify; there is no delete, rename, copy, symlink, gitlink, type change or executable-mode drift, and the single executable path was already executable at main. The four changed control objects are byte-identical at the anchor and at HEAD and equal the exact bytes that received an independent PASS in Materialization V2; the runner and both fixtures are unchanged from main, proven by their absence from the complete reconstructed diff, though their bytes are not shipped here. Review 05 is exact at 57 of 57 C5 checks with independence, static and dynamic all PASS, candidate PASS and bootstrap BLOCKED; implementation evidence 06 is exact with all four stage phases at floor D and PASS, and its two stages map precisely onto ledger commits 10 and 11. All twelve evidence objects are valid JSON, introduced exactly once as adds, never subsequently modified, and linked from R2_STATE by both path and exact digest. The commit history is a strictly linear thirteen-commit single-parent chain from main to HEAD with no merge commits, no path touched outside the bootstrap inventory, and a per-commit replay that reproduces the full record set exactly. The admin tail is exactly R2_STATE.md modified plus implementation evidence 06 added. The floor-D classification was reproduced from first principles by executing the reviewed checker against an independently reconstructed diff, matching the recorded result per path; running it at classes A, B and C returned FAIL with exit 3 and only class D passed, which establishes that the authorized class is an external input rather than something the gate grants itself, so the classification is factual and not self-authorization. Thirty-eight adversarial scenarios were exercised, the six supplied probes plus thirty-two designed independently by this reviewer, including length-preserving evidence tampering, tampering with the R2_STATE ledger repaired to stay internally self-consistent, review 05 disposition and check-count downgrades, control-byte drift at and after the anchor, symlink, gitlink, type-change, rename, delete and executable-bit entries, nested .gitattributes CRLF lockout, Unicode homoglyph and non-UTF-8 path injection, workflow extension twinning, runner and fixture tampering, evidence touched three times with net-zero effect, non-linear merge commits and commit-order permutation. Every one was rejected. The single acceptance was a two-commit tail producing a byte-identical final tree and identical cumulative diff, which is an equivalence rather than a false green and is recorded as NB-05. No false green was found. There are no blocking findings and seven non-blocking ones, the most substantive being that three of the seven reviewed objects ship no bytes, that merge-tree equality is established by deduction rather than recomputation because the full tree is absent, and that real repository state is a supplied claim. R2AA-012 stays OPEN, with zero workflow runs recorded at both the anchor and HEAD confirming no check run has ever bound to any SHA; DC-006 stays OPEN and IR2-002 stays blocking before the first functional task. Disposition is PASS as evidence only. It justifies opening a separate Human Gate D on the bootstrap merge and nothing more: it does not authorize the merge itself, branch protection, required checks, rulesets, any GitHub settings change, or entry into R2-5.
